- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

3	In the calculus of evaluation design an RL environment is an evaluation
4	record whose judgment is fed back into the controller roster every

11	   the step-outcome record, ordered by refinement where they are comparable;
12	   the number of distinct images bounds what one episode can tell the loop.

96	def episodes_to_distinguish(kernel: dict[str, dict[str, Q]], hypotheses: int) -> int:
97	    """Fewest episodes of this channel after which ``hypotheses`` alternatives
98	    could all be told apart.  Counting bound: ``images ** episodes`` outcomes
99	    must cover the hypotheses.  A one-image channel distinguishes nothing."""
100	
101	    if type(hypotheses) is not int or hypotheses < 1:
102	        raise ValueError("hypotheses must be a positive integer")
103	    images = image_count(kernel)
104	    if hypotheses == 1:
105	        return 0
106	    if images == 1:
107	        raise ValueError("a one-image channel cannot distinguish hypotheses")
108	    episodes, reach = 0, 1
109	    while reach < hypotheses:
110	        episodes += 1

112	    return episodes

117	def score_query_lower_bound(items: int, failed: int) -> int:
118	    """Fewest score queries that could identify which ``failed`` of ``items``
119	    fail, once the failure count is known.
120	
121	    A query names a subset to patch and returns how many of its items were
122	    failing, one of ``failed + 1`` values; ``q`` queries distinguish at most
123	    ``(failed + 1) ** q`` failure sets, and there are ``comb(items, failed)``.
124	    """
125	
126	    if type(items) is not int or type(failed) is not int or items < 1 or not 0 <= failed <= items:
127	        raise ValueError("items must be positive and 0 <= failed <= items")
128	    targets = comb(items, failed)
129	    queries, reach = 0, 1
130	    while reach < targets:
131	        queries += 1
132	        reach *= failed + 1
133	    return queries

136	def binary_splitting(items: int, failed: frozenset[int]) -> tuple[frozenset[int], int]:
137	    """Identify the failed set by recursive halving.  Returns the recovered set
138	    and the number of score queries used, counting the first query that
139	    reveals the failure count."""
140	
141	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1 or not failed <= frozenset(range(items)):
142	        raise ValueError("failed must be a subset of range(items)")
143	    queries = 0
144	    found: set[int] = set()
145	
146	    def count(subset: frozenset[int]) -> int:
147	        nonlocal queries
148	        queries += 1
149	        return len(failed & subset)
150	
151	    def search(subset: frozenset[int], known: int) -> None:
152	        if known == 0:
153	            return
154	        if known == len(subset):
155	            found.update(subset)
156	            return
157	        ordered = sorted(subset)
158	        left = frozenset(ordered[: len(ordered) // 2])
159	        right = frozenset(ordered[len(ordered) // 2:])
160	        left_count = count(left)
161	        search(left, left_count)
162	        search(right, known - left_count)
163	
164	    everything = frozenset(range(items))
165	    search(everything, count(everything))
166	    return frozenset(found), queries

169	def binary_splitting_worst_case(items: int, failed: int) -> int:
170	    """Most queries binary splitting uses over every failure set of that size."""
171	
172	    if type(items) is not int or type(failed) is not int or items < 1 or not 0 <= failed <= items:
173	        raise ValueError("items must be positive and 0 <= failed <= items")
174	    worst = 0
175	    for subset in combinations(range(items), failed):
176	        recovered, used = binary_splitting(items, frozenset(subset))
177	        if recovered != frozenset(subset):
178	            raise AssertionError("binary splitting failed to recover a set")
179	        worst = max(worst, used)
180	    return worst

183	def exact_min_queries(items: int, failed: int) -> int:
184	    """Minimax number of score queries, after the failure count is known, that
185	    an adaptive strategy needs to identify the failed set.  Exhaustive over
186	    strategies; feasible only for small ``items``."""
187	
188	    if type(items) is not int or type(failed) is not int or not 1 <= items <= 7 or not 0 <= failed <= items:
189	        raise ValueError("items must lie in 1..7 and 0 <= failed <= items")
190	    subsets = [frozenset(s) for size in range(1, items) for s in combinations(range(items), size)]
191	
192	    def counting_bound(candidates: int) -> int:
193	        queries, reach = 0, 1
194	        while reach < candidates:
195	            queries += 1
196	            reach *= failed + 1
197	        return queries

199	    @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
200	    def solve(candidates: frozenset[frozenset[int]]) -> int:
201	        if len(candidates) <= 1:
202	            return 0
203	        bound = counting_bound(len(candidates))
204	        best = None
205	        for subset in subsets:
206	            groups: dict[int, list[frozenset[int]]] = {}
207	            for candidate in candidates:
208	                groups.setdefault(len(candidate & subset), []).append(candidate)
209	            if len(groups) == 1:
210	                continue
211	            worst = 1 + max(solve(frozenset(group)) for group in groups.values())
212	            if best is None or worst < best:
213	                best = worst
214	            if best == bound:
215	                break
216	        return best
217	
218	    return solve(frozenset(frozenset(c) for c in combinations(range(items), failed)))

223	def shared_error_bounds(accuracy: Q, judge_error: Q) -> tuple[Q, Q]:
224	    """Feasible range of ``eps1``, the judge's error rate on items the
225	    controller gets wrong, given the controller's accuracy and the judge's
226	    marginal error rate ``judge_error = a * eps0 + (1 - a) * eps1``."""
227	
228	    if not 0 < accuracy < 1 or not 0 <= judge_error <= 1:
229	        raise ValueError("accuracy must lie strictly inside (0, 1) and judge_error in [0, 1]")
230	    low = max(Q(0), (judge_error - accuracy) / (1 - accuracy))
231	    high = min(Q(1), judge_error / (1 - accuracy))
232	    return low, high
233

235	def observed_accuracy_shared(accuracy: Q, judge_error: Q, eps1: Q) -> Q:
236	    """Observed accuracy against a binary judge whose error rate is ``eps1`` on
237	    the controller's wrong answers and ``eps0`` on its right ones, with the
238	    marginal error held at ``judge_error``.  Binary labels: a wrong judge on a
239	    wrong answer marks it correct."""
240	
241	    low, high = shared_error_bounds(accuracy, judge_error)
242	    if not low <= eps1 <= high:
243	        raise ValueError("eps1 is infeasible for the marginal judge error")
244	    eps0 = (judge_error - (1 - accuracy) * eps1) / accuracy
245	    return accuracy * (1 - eps0) + (1 - accuracy) * eps1
246

248	def judge_correlation_inflation(accuracy: Q, judge_error: Q, eps1: Q) -> Q:
249	    """Observed accuracy under shared errors minus observed accuracy under
250	    independent errors.  Identity: ``2 (1 - a) (eps1 - judge_error)``."""
251	
252	    return observed_accuracy_shared(accuracy, judge_error, eps1) - observed_accuracy(accuracy, judge_error)

255	def ceiling_reachable_without_memorization(accuracy: Q, judge_error: Q) -> bool:
256	    """True iff some feasible ``eps1`` lifts observed accuracy to the noise
257	    ceiling ``1 - judge_error``.  That happens exactly at ``eps1 >= 1/2``, so
258	    the condition is ``judge_error >= (1 - accuracy) / 2``."""
259	
260	    if not judge_error < Q(1, 2):
261	        raise ValueError("the ceiling 1 - eps presumes eps below one half")
262	    _, high = shared_error_bounds(accuracy, judge_error)
263	    return high >= Q(1, 2)

268	def selection_value(kernel: dict[str, dict[str, Q]], types: dict[str, dict[str, Q]],
269	                    prior: dict[str, Q], utility: dict[str, Q]) -> Q:
270	    """Bayes value of keeping one of two candidates, each of an independent
271	    type drawn from ``prior``, after seeing each candidate's channel image.
272	    ``types`` maps a type to its record distribution; the kept candidate pays
273	    its type's utility."""
274	
275	    if set(types) != set(prior) or set(types) != set(utility):
276	        raise ValueError("types, prior and utility must name the same types")
277	    if sum(prior.values()) != 1 or any(p < 0 for p in prior.values()):
278	        raise ValueError("prior must be a distribution")
279	    for distribution in types.values():
280	        if sum(distribution.values()) != 1 or any(p < 0 for p in distribution.values()):
281	            raise ValueError("each type needs a record distribution")
282	        if not set(distribution) <= set(kernel):
283	            raise ValueError("records must lie in the kernel's domain")
284	    gain: dict[tuple[str, str], list[Q]] = {}
285	    for first, second in product(types, repeat=2):
286	        for record_1, p_1 in types[first].items():
287	            for record_2, p_2 in types[second].items():
288	                weight = prior[first] * p_1 * prior[second] * p_2
289	                if weight == 0:
290	                    continue
291	                observation = (_image(kernel[record_1]), _image(kernel[record_2]))
292	                entry = gain.setdefault(observation, [Q(0), Q(0)])
293	                entry[0] += weight * utility[first]
294	                entry[1] += weight * utility[second]
295	    return sum((max(entry) for entry in gain.values()), Q(0))

133	def _value_by_enumerating_rules(kernel, types, prior, utility):
134	    image = {record: next(iter(kernel[record])) for record in kernel}
135	    weights = {}
136	    for first, second in product(types, repeat=2):
137	        for r1, p1 in types[first].items():
138	            for r2, p2 in types[second].items():
139	                key = (image[r1], image[r2])
140	                weights.setdefault(key, [Q(0), Q(0)])
141	                weights[key][0] += prior[first] * p1 * prior[second] * p2 * utility[first]
142	                weights[key][1] += prior[first] * p1 * prior[second] * p2 * utility[second]
143	    observations = sorted(weights)
144	    best = None
145	    for rule in product((0, 1), repeat=len(observations)):
146	        total = sum((weights[o][choice] for o, choice in zip(observations, rule)), Q(0))
147	        best = total if best is None or total > best else best
148	    return best

1	# The selection gap across generations, exactly
2	
3	Draft 0.2 — 2026-10-13 (0.1: 2026-10-12). Companion to `evaluation_feedback_insertions.md`,
4	whose selection law stops at one generation and whose multi-generation rows come from seeded
5	JavaScript. This note replaces the accumulation claim with a finite Markov chain in exact
6	arithmetic. No model is called; nothing here is evidence about any controller. Evidence levels
7	follow the calculus card (§11): *algebraic identity* (every parameter), *finite verified
8	example* (enumerated cells only), *synthetic mechanism result* (a property of this toy chain).
9	Version 0.2 adds a proven bound in place of §2's extreme-value remark (Prop. 5), an exact chain
10	for item-correlated candidates (§5, Prop. 6), and the one-generation gate-versus-naive theorem
11	under true gains (§6, Prop. 7).
12	
13	Source `src/spiral_ln/evaluation_feedback_multigen.py`; 112 tests in `tests/`; receipt
14	`output/evaluation_feedback_multigen/multigen_v0_2.json` (56 checks, source hashes, exact
15	fractions, float renderings under `headline`). Bounds involving \(\ln\) or \(\sqrt{}\) are
16	floats, compared with exact values under an absolute tolerance of \(10^{-12}\).
17	
18	```powershell
19	$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
20	python scripts/verify_evaluation_feedback_multigen.py --output output/evaluation_feedback_multigen/multigen_v0_2.json
21	python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_feedback_multigen.py -q

23	
24	## 1. The chain: vertices, edges, policy
25	
26	A reused set of \(n\) items. **State**: the incumbent's realized count \(c\in\{0,\dots,n\}\) on
27	that set. Each generation draws \(K\) candidates i.i.d. and independent of the incumbent,
28	\(C_k\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\), \(M=\max_k C_k\). **Actions**: accept or reject the best candidate.
29	**Policy**: accept iff \(M>c+t(c)\), \(t:\{0..n\}\to\mathbb N\). **Edges**: \(c\to j\) with
30	probability \(P(M=j)\) for \(j>c+t(c)\); the self-loop carries \(F(c+t(c))^K\), \(F\) the binomial
31	CDF with \(F(j)=1\) for \(j\ge n\). The graph is a DAG of upward edges plus self-loops; its sinks
32	\(\{c:c+t(c)\ge n\}\) are the absorbing states. Initial state \(c_0\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\).
33	Reported score \(c_G/n\); readout value \(p\); readout gap \(\rho_G=\mathbb E[c_G]/n-p\). In the
34	calculus: \(\operatorname{Repeat}_G\) of one generation with carry map "keep \(c\)", composed
35	with \(\operatorname{Feedback}_{s,\text{score-only}}\) whose consumer selects among candidates.
36	
37	**Gate discretization.** `sim.js` accepts iff \(M>c+z\sqrt{p(1-p)/n}\,n\) with \(p=c/n\), i.e.
38	\(M-c>z\sqrt{c(n-c)/n}\). The difference is an integer \(d\), and \(d>x\) iff
39	\(d\ge\lfloor x\rfloor+1\), so \(t(c)=\lfloor z\sqrt{c(n-c)/n}\rfloor\), computed exactly as
40	\(\lfloor\sqrt{a/b}\rfloor=\mathrm{isqrt}(ab)\,//\,b\). For \(n=16,z=3\):
41	\(t=(0,2,3,4,5,5,5,5,6,5,5,5,5,4,3,2,0)\). Fixture `gate_threshold`, checked by
42	\(t^2\le z^2c(n-c)/n<(t+1)^2\) on every state and against the real-valued rule for every
43	integer \(d\). Algebraic identity.
44	
45	## 2. Naive reuse is a running maximum
46	
47	**Proposition 1.** With \(t\equiv0\), \(c_G=\max(c_0,M_1,\dots,M_G)\), the maximum of \(GK+1\)
48	i.i.d. \(\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\) draws, so \(\rho_G=\) `selection_inflation(n, GK+1, p).readout_gap`.
49	The initial incumbent is one draw because it is scored on the reused set like every candidate;
50	a *known* count \(c_0\) gives \(\mathbb E[\max(c_0,X)]\), \(X\) the max of \(GK\) draws
51	(`running_max_from_point`). *Proof.* If \(M_g>c_{g-1}\) the policy sets
52	\(c_g=M_g=\max(c_{g-1},M_g)\); otherwise \(c_g=c_{g-1}=\max(c_{g-1},M_g)\). Induct. Algebraic
53	identity. The DP equals the closed form on all 18 null cells (\(n\in\{4,8,16\}\),
54	\(K\in\{1,2,4\}\), \(p\in\{\tfrac12,\tfrac14\}\), \(G=0..20\)); at \(n=2,K=2,G=2\) it equals
55	literal enumeration of all \(2^{10}\) item outcomes.
56	
57	**Consequences.** (i) \(\rho_G\) is non-decreasing in \(G\): a maximum over more draws is
58	pointwise larger. (ii) Increments are non-increasing: \(a_{m+1}-a_m=\mathbb E[(X-M_m)^+]\) with
59	\(M_m\) pointwise non-decreasing in \(m\). (iii) \(P(c_G=n)=1-(1-p^n)^{GK+1}\), so for fixed
60	\(n\) and \(0<p<1\), \(\rho_G\uparrow1-p\): bounded by the lattice, never stationary. These are
61	algebraic identities with the proofs above; the fixture verifies them on the enumerated cells
62	only.
63	
64	**Proposition 5 (bounds).** For every \(n,K,p,G\), with \(m=GK+1\) and \(\sigma^2=np(1-p)\),
65	\[\rho_G\le\sqrt{\tfrac{\ln m}{2n}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad
66	\rho_G\le\sqrt{\tfrac{2p(1-p)\ln m}{n}}+\tfrac{\ln m}{3n}.\]
67	*Proof.* \(Y_i=X_i-np\) is a sum of \(n\) centred Bernoullis, each in an interval of length
68	one, so Hoeffding's lemma and independence give \(\mathbb E e^{\lambda Y_i}\le e^{\lambda^2n/8}\).
69	The maximal inequality \(\mathbb E\max_iY_i\le\lambda^{-1}\ln\sum_i\mathbb E e^{\lambda Y_i}\)
70	(Jensen, then \(\max\le\sum\)) gives \(\mathbb E\max_iY_i\le(\ln m)/\lambda+\lambda n/8\), and
71	\(\lambda=\sqrt{8\ln m/n}\) makes this \(\sqrt{n\ln m/2}\); divide by \(n\). For the second
72	bound, a centred variable with \(|Z|\le1\) and variance \(v\) has
73	\(\ln\mathbb E e^{\lambda Z}\le v(e^\lambda-1-\lambda)\le\lambda^2v/(2(1-\lambda/3))\) for
74	\(\lambda<3\); summed over items \(v=\sigma^2\), and the same maximal inequality with
75	\(\lambda^{-1}=\tfrac13+\sqrt{\sigma^2/(2\ln m)}\) gives \(\sqrt{2\sigma^2\ln m}+\tfrac13\ln m\)
76	(Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart, Cor. 2.6). Algebraic identity. Both bounds grow without limit in
77	\(G\) while \(\rho_G\le1-p\), so they are loose at fixed \(n\) for large \(G\); the Hoeffding
78	bound passes \(1-p\) at \(G=7,4,2\) for \(n=4,p=\tfrac12,K=1,2,4\) and at \(G=14\) for
79	\(n=8,K=4\). At \(p=\tfrac12\) the Hoeffding bound equals the Gaussian scale
80	\(\sqrt{2p(1-p)\ln m/n}\) of the old remark and Bernstein exceeds it by \(\ln m/(3n)\);
81	Bernstein is tighter only for small \(p(1-p)\) and \(\ln m/n\) (here \(p=\tfrac14,n=16,m\le3\):
82	3 of 360 cell-generations). Finite table (`bound_fixture`, 18 cells \(\times\) 21 generations):
83	both bounds hold everywhere; the ratio \(\rho_G/\sqrt{2p(1-p)\ln m/n}\) runs from 0.453 to
84	0.886 at \(G\in\{1,5,10,20\}\), rising in \(G\) and in \(n\). At \(n=8,K=2,p=\tfrac12\): exact
85	\(0.147,.273,.321,.365\); Hoeffding \(0.262,.387,.436,.482\); ratio \(0.56,.70,.74,.76\). At
86	\(n=16,K=4,p=\tfrac12\): exact \(0.144,\dots,.295\); Hoeffding \(0.224,\dots,.371\); ratio
87	\(0.64\to0.80\). The Gaussian scale is an upper envelope on every cell, not an approximation.
88	
89	## 3. Fresh blocks
90	
91	**Proposition 2.** (a) If each generation scores incumbent and candidates on a fresh block and
92	reports on a second fresh block, the expected reported score is \(p\) at every generation: the
93	readout block is independent of whatever selected the controller, and under the null every
94	controller has probability \(p\). (b) If it reports on the selection block, the reported count
95	at \(g\ge1\) is \(M\) if \(M>I+t(I)\), else \(I\), with \(I\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\) the
96	incumbent's fresh count; the law does not depend on \(g\). For \(t\equiv0\) it is \(\max(I,M)\),
97	the maximum of \(K+1\) draws, so the gap equals `selection_inflation(n, K+1, p)` at every
98	\(g\ge1\) and does not accumulate. Both algebraic identities (independence, linearity);
99	verified on 12 cells and by enumeration at \(n=2,K=2\) in both modes. The reused chain
100	coincides with (b) at \(G=1\) for any gate and exceeds it strictly for \(G\ge2\) on every
101	enumerated cell (finite check).
102	
103	## 4. The gate
104	
105	**Proposition 3 (false acceptance).** From state \(c\) the generation accepts with probability
106	\(\alpha(c)=1-F(\min(n,c+t(c)))^K\); under the null every acceptance is false, and the
107	unconditional rate at generation \(g\) is \(\sum_c\pi_{g-1}(c)\alpha(c)\). Algebraic identity.
108	For \(n=16,K=4,z=3\): \(\alpha(8)=1-(1-17/65536)^4\approx1.0\times10^{-3}\); naive \(\approx0.36\).
109	
110	**Proposition 4 (gate dominance, null only).** For any \(t\ge0\), couple the gated and naive
111	chains on the same draws. The gated state always belongs to \(\{c_0,M_1,\dots,M_g\}\), whose
112	maximum is the naive state; hence \(c^t_G\le c^0_G\) pointwise, \(\rho^t_G\le\rho^0_G\), and
113	\(\alpha^t(c)\le\alpha^0(c)\). Algebraic identity by coupling; its hypothesis is that every
114	candidate's law is the same whatever the history, i.e. the null. With true gains it fails and
115	can reverse (§6). Values at \(G=20,p=\tfrac12,n=16,K=4\): naive \(0.2947\); \(z=1\): \(0.2723\);
116	\(z=2\): \(0.2019\); \(z=3\): \(0.1328\); expected false acceptances \(2.34\to0.33\).
117	\(n=8,K=2\): naive \(0.3645\), \(z=3\): \(0.0967\). The gate also creates sinks below the
118	ceiling: for \(n=8,z=3\) states \(4..8\) absorb, so a gated loop freezes; the simulation's
119	GATED arm accepting 0–2% of generations is the same mechanism.
120	
121	## 5. Correlated candidates: the mutation chain
122	
123	`sim.js` perturbs the incumbent's per-item quirks, so each candidate is correlated with the
124	incumbent item by item. Exact model: on each item, independently, a candidate copies the
125	incumbent's outcome with probability \(1-q\) and redraws it as Bernoulli(\(p\)) with probability
126	\(q\). Marginally a candidate is still \(\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\), with per-item correlation \(1-q\)
127	to the incumbent. The map from \(\sin\phi=0.2\) to \(q\) is not exact: the rotation acts on
128	latent quirks, not on outcomes, and no \(q\) reproduces its conditional count law.
129	
130	**Proposition 6.** Given incumbent count \(c\), a candidate's count is \(c-L+U\) with
131	\(L\sim\mathrm{Bin}(c,q(1-p))\), \(U\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n-c,qp)\) independent, because a right item
132	is lost iff it is redrawn and fails and a wrong item is gained iff it is redrawn and succeeds;
133	the law depends on the incumbent's outcome vector only through \(c\) since items are
134	exchangeable and the perturbation is item-symmetric, so with \(K\) conditionally i.i.d.
135	candidates and the same policy the process is again a Markov chain on \(c\)
136	(`mutation_candidate_law`, `mutation_transition_kernel`). (a) \(q=1\) gives
137	\(\mathrm{Bin}(c,p)+\mathrm{Bin}(n-c,p)=\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)\): the independent chain, exactly.
138	(b) \(q=0\) gives the point mass at \(c\): nothing is ever accepted, \(\rho_G=0\). (c) For
139	every \(q\), acceptance requires \(M>c+t(c)\ge c\), so \(c_g\) is pointwise non-decreasing,
140	\(\rho_G\) is non-decreasing in \(G\), and \(\rho_G\le1-p\). (d) From \(c=n-1\) a candidate
141	reaches \(n\) with probability \(qp(1-q(1-p))^{n-1}\), maximal at \(q=1/(n(1-p))\) and
142	decreasing beyond it, so the kernel is not monotone in \(q\) state by state and no coupling
143	in \(q\) exists. All algebraic identities; (a) is checked as equality of the whole state law
144	on every null cell under naive and \(z=1\) policies, (b)–(d) on the same cells, and the DP
145	matches enumeration of outcome *vectors* at \(n=2,K=2,G=2\) and \(n=3,K=2,G=1\) (which tests
146	the Markov-on-count claim itself). Proposition 1 has no analogue: the candidate law moves
147	with the state, so \(c_G\) is not a running maximum of i.i.d. draws.
148	
149	**Monotonicity in \(q\), finite survey** (\(q\in\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12,\tfrac34,1\}\), 18 null
150	cells, naive and \(z=1\)). \(\rho_1\) is non-decreasing in \(q\) on every cell: correlation
151	lowers the first-generation inflation. \(\rho_G\) is **not** monotone in \(q\) on any naive
152	cell (first failure at \(G=2\)–5) and on 15 of 18 gated cells; at \(G=20\) every \(q<1\) gives a
153	*larger* gap than \(q=1\) on every naive cell with \(n\ge8\), and \(q=\tfrac12\) does on all 18.
154	\(n=8,K=2,p=\tfrac12\), naive: \(\rho_1=0,.074,.109,.132,.147\) and
155	\(\rho_{20}=0,.455,.447,.409,.365\) for the five \(q\). \(n=16,K=4\): \(\rho_{20}=0,.445,.395,.342,.295\).
156	Mechanism: a mutated candidate starts from the incumbent's already-overfit vector and need
157	only flip one wrong item without losing a right one, so improvements keep arriving when an
158	independent redraw would almost never beat an inflated \(c\); the chain hill-climbs the fixed
159	item set. What this says about `sim.js`: its correlation lowers each generation's inflation
160	from a *fresh* state but raises the accumulated gap over twenty generations; the earlier
161	boundary remark that correlation "lowers every per-generation inflation" was wrong beyond
162	\(G=1\). Synthetic mechanism result on these cells.
163	
164	## 6. True gains: the drift chain
165	
166	State \((c,i)\) with \(p(i)=\min(1,\tfrac14+i/8)\). Each candidate draws a gain multiple \(m\)
167	from a law (constant, or one law per generation), has probability \(p(i+m)\), and on acceptance
168	the state becomes \((M,i+m^*)\), \(m^*\) the accepted candidate's gain; by exchangeability
169	\(P(M=j,m^*=m)=P(M=j)\,q_m\,\mathrm{Bin}(n,p(i+m))(j)/\mathrm{mix}(j)\). Reported
170	\(\mathbb E[c_g]/n\), true \(\mathbb E[p(i_g)]\), phantom share \(1-\)true gain/reported gain.
171	Verified by enumeration of every gain draw and item outcome at \(n=2,K=2,G=2\) (six laws, two
172	policies); the zero-gain law reproduces the null chain exactly (test). Laws: *fixed*
173	\(\delta=\tfrac18\); *two-point* \(\delta=\tfrac18\) w.p. \(\tfrac14\); *decaying two-point*
174	\(q_g=\tfrac14(\tfrac34)^{g-1}\), a lattice analogue of the simulation's \(0.06\cdot0.95^{g-1}\).
175	Cells \((n,K)\in\{(4,2),(4,4),(8,2),(8,4),(16,2)\}\), \(G=20\), naive and \(z=1\). Everything
176	below is a synthetic mechanism result on those cells and nothing more.
177	
178	- Two-point, naive, \(n=8,K=2\): reported \(0.778\), true \(0.420\); phantom share \(0.678\)
179	  over \(0..20\), \(0.711\) early half, \(0.504\) late half; late/early gain ratio reported
180	  \(0.195\), true \(0.334\).

1	"""Exact, synthetic checks for judgment-to-controller feedback.
2	
3	Nothing in this module calls a model, trains a learner, or runs an improvement
4	loop.  It types the channel by which a judgment reaches the process that
5	produces the next controller, and keeps the resulting *readout gap* separate
6	from baseline gain, robust regret, discrimination gap, and exploitability.
7	
8	Three access classes order that channel.  ``sealed`` returns nothing,
9	``score_only`` returns an aggregate count, ``item_level`` returns per-item
10	outcomes.  Each is a deterministic coarsening of the next, so the finite
11	data-processing inequality used for observation-only Hide applies to what the
12	loop can learn about its own failures.
13	"""
14

16	
17	from dataclasses import dataclass
18	from fractions import Fraction as Q
19	from itertools import product
20	from math import comb
21	
22	from spiral_ln.evaluation_game_testbed import _pushforward, _tv
23	
24	ACCESS_CLASSES = ("sealed", "score_only", "item_level")
25	ROLES = ("selection", "readout")
26	EVENT_KINDS = ("score_query", "item_feedback", "readout")
27	
28	
29	def access_kernel(access: str, items: int) -> dict[str, dict[str, Q]]:
30	    """Deterministic feedback kernel from per-item outcome records.
31	
32	    A record is a string of ``0``/``1`` of length ``items``.  The kernel says
33	    what reaches the loop, not what the evaluator stores.
34	    """
35	
36	    if access not in ACCESS_CLASSES:
37	        raise ValueError("unknown access class")
38	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1:
39	        raise ValueError("items must be a positive integer")
40	    kernel = {}
41	    for bits in product("01", repeat=items):
42	        record = "".join(bits)
43	        if access == "sealed":
44	            image = "sealed"
45	        elif access == "score_only":
46	            image = f"score={record.count('1')}"
47	        else:
48	            image = record
49	        kernel[record] = {image: Q(1)}
50	    return kernel
51	
52	
53	def access_order_fixture() -> dict[str, object]:
54	    """Two controllers with equal scores and different failures.
55	
56	    Item-level feedback separates them completely; score-only feedback cannot
57	    separate them at all.  A second pair with different scores is separated by
58	    both, and no pair is separated through a sealed set.
59	    """
60	
61	    same_score = ({"10": Q(1)}, {"01": Q(1)})
62	    different_score = ({"11": Q(1)}, {"00": Q(1)})
63	    gaps = {}
64	    for name, (left, right) in (("same_score", same_score),
65	                                ("different_score", different_score)):
66	        gaps[name] = {
67	            access: _tv(_pushforward(left, access_kernel(access, 2)),
68	                        _pushforward(right, access_kernel(access, 2)))
69	            for access in ACCESS_CLASSES
70	        }
71	    ordered = all(g["sealed"] <= g["score_only"] <= g["item_level"] for g in gaps.values())
72	    return {"operator_type": "judgment_to_controller_feedback_kernel",
73	            "gaps": gaps, "access_classes_ordered_by_coarsening": ordered,
74	            "acts_between_generations": True, "changes_recorded_evidence": False}
75

78	    return [Q(comb(n, j)) * p**j * (1 - p)**(n - j) for j in range(n + 1)]

70	> Total-variation distance between two controllers' feedback therefore cannot
71	> increase from item-level to score-only to sealed. Two controllers that fail
72	> different items with equal totals are separated completely by item-level
73	> feedback and not at all by a score.

79	
80	> Keeping the best of \(K\) candidates by score on \(s\), then reporting that
81	> score, overstates: \(\mathbb E[\max_k\hat S_k]\ge\max_k\mathbb E[\hat S_k]\).
82	> This is the same convexity as the mixture law, with the candidate index in
83	> place of the mixture component. For candidates of equal true value

100	> predictor blind to the flips exceeds \(1-\varepsilon\) in expectation on
101	> observed labels. Let \(v\) be the controller's observed accuracy before any
102	> item of \(s\) is memorized. If it memorizes a share \(m/n\) of \(s\) chosen
103	> without regard to its outcomes, it scores \(m/n+(1-m/n)v\) on \(s\) and
104	> crosses the ceiling only when \(m/n>(1-\varepsilon-v)/(1-v)\). If it memorizes
105	> items it failed, which is what item-level feedback supplies, it scores
106	> \(v+m/n\) and crosses when \(m/n>1-\varepsilon-v\): the same threshold
107	> \((1-\varepsilon-v)/(1-v)\), now as a share of the failed items. Below the

from fractions import Fraction as Q
from itertools import product
from math import atan, log, pi, sqrt

import pytest

from spiral_ln.evaluation_feedback_multigen import best_of_pmf
from spiral_ln.evaluation_selection_kl import (
    GRID_P, LOG_TOLERANCE, SUPREMUM_TOLERANCE, TIE_RULES, beirami_radius, binomial_records,
    binomial_score_law, brute_force_selected_law, conditioned_on_max_law, dv_bound,
    first_index_weight, gaussian_max_expectation, gaussian_ratio_limit, gap_to_bound_ratio,
    hoeffding_proxy, kearns_saul_proxy, kl_ball_supremum, kl_divergence, kl_max_law, max_law,
    score_law, selected_record_law, selection_gap, subgaussian_violation, uniform_distinct_scores_kl,
    uniform_weight, verify,
)

HALF, QUARTER = Q(1, 2), Q(1, 4)

SPACES = [
    ({"a": Q(1), "b": Q(0)}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}),
    ({"a": Q(1, 3), "b": Q(2, 3)}, {"a": 0, "b": 0}),
    ({"a": Q(1, 2), "b": Q(1, 4), "c": Q(1, 8), "d": Q(1, 8)}, {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 1, "d": 2}),
    ({"a": Q(1, 5), "b": Q(1, 5), "c": Q(1, 5), "d": Q(2, 5)}, {"a": 3, "b": 3, "c": 3, "d": 3}),
    ({"w": Q(1, 10), "x": Q(3, 10), "y": Q(2, 5), "z": Q(1, 5)}, {"w": Q(1, 2), "x": -1, "y": Q(1, 2), "z": 7}),
]


def _enumerate(p0, score, candidates, rule):
    """Independent enumeration over index tuples; the tie rule is applied literally."""

    records = list(p0)
    law = {record: Q(0) for record in records}
    for indices in product(range(len(records)), repeat=candidates):
        weight = Q(1)
        for i in indices:
            weight *= p0[records[i]]
        if weight == 0:
            continue
        top = max(score[records[i]] for i in indices)
        winners = [pos for pos, i in enumerate(indices) if score[records[i]] == top]
        if rule == "first_index":
            law[records[indices[winners[0]]]] += weight
        else:
            share = weight / len(winners)
            for pos in winners:
                law[records[indices[pos]]] += share
    return law


@pytest.mark.parametrize("p0,score", SPACES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("candidates", [1, 2, 3])
def test_tie_rules_match_enumeration_and_each_other(p0, score, candidates):
    conditioned = conditioned_on_max_law(p0, score, candidates)
    for rule in TIE_RULES:
        closed = selected_record_law(p0, score, candidates, rule)
        assert closed == _enumerate(p0, score, candidates, rule)
        assert closed == brute_force_selected_law(p0, score, candidates, rule)
        assert closed == conditioned
        assert sum(closed.values()) == 1


def test_weights_agree_with_the_geometric_identity():
    for below, upto in ((Q(0), Q(1)), (Q(1, 3), Q(1, 2)), (Q(2, 7), Q(9, 10)), (Q(0), Q(1, 5))):
        for candidates in range(1, 7):
            direct = (upto**candidates - below**candidates) / (upto - below)
            assert first_index_weight(below, upto, candidates) == direct
            assert uniform_weight(below, upto, candidates) == direct


def test_max_law_matches_multigen_best_of_pmf():
    for items, candidates, p in ((2, 2, HALF), (3, 4, QUARTER), (5, 3, Q(2, 3)), (8, 1, HALF)):
        law = max_law(binomial_score_law(items, p), candidates)
        assert [law[Q(j, items)] for j in range(items + 1)] == best_of_pmf(items, candidates, p)
        assert sum(law.values()) == 1


def test_kl_on_records_equals_kl_of_max_law_and_gap_matches_selection_inflation():
    for items in range(1, 7):
        for candidates in (2, 3, 4):
            for p in (HALF, QUARTER, Q(9, 10)):
                p0, score = binomial_records(items, p)
                law = selected_record_law(p0, score, candidates)
                assert abs(kl_divergence(law, p0) - kl_max_law(items, candidates, p)) <= LOG_TOLERANCE
                gap = sum((mass * score[r] for r, mass in law.items()), Q(0)) - p
                assert gap == selection_gap(items, candidates, p)


def test_data_processing_inequality_by_direct_computation():
    p0 = {"a": Q(1, 2), "b": Q(1, 4), "c": Q(1, 8), "d": Q(1, 8)}
    score = {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 1, "d": 2}
    for candidates in (2, 3):
        discrete = selected_record_law(p0, score, candidates)
        discrete_kl = kl_divergence(discrete, p0)
        previous = -1.0
        for levels in (1, 2, 3, 5, 8):
            joint_p0 = {(r, l): m / levels for r, m in p0.items() for l in range(levels)}
            joint_score = {(r, l): Q(score[r]) + Q(l + 1, 2 * (levels + 1)) for (r, l) in joint_p0}
            joint = selected_record_law(joint_p0, joint_score, candidates)
            marginal = {r: Q(0) for r in p0}
            for (r, _), m in joint.items():
                marginal[r] += m
            assert marginal == discrete
            joint_kl = kl_divergence(joint, joint_p0)
            assert joint_kl >= discrete_kl - LOG_TOLERANCE
            assert joint_kl > previous
            assert joint_kl < beirami_radius(candidates)
            previous = joint_kl
        assert beirami_radius(candidates) - previous < 0.01
    # the same inequality for a pair of laws unrelated to selection
    joint_a = {("x", 0): Q(1, 2), ("x", 1): Q(1, 6), ("y", 0): Q(1, 6), ("y", 1): Q(1, 6)}
    joint_b = {("x", 0): Q(1, 4), ("x", 1): Q(1, 4), ("y", 0): Q(1, 4), ("y", 1): Q(1, 4)}
    marginal_a = {"x": Q(2, 3), "y": Q(1, 3)}
    marginal_b = {"x": Q(1, 2), "y": Q(1, 2)}
    assert kl_divergence(marginal_a, marginal_b) <= kl_divergence(joint_a, joint_b)


def test_n_equals_1_gap_equals_kl_ball_supremum_exactly_via_the_tilt():
    for candidates in (2, 3, 5, 10, 20):
        for p in GRID_P:
            top = 1 - (1 - p)**candidates
            assert selection_gap(1, candidates, p) == top - p
            kl = kl_max_law(1, candidates, p)
            binary = float(top) * log(float(top / p)) + float(1 - top) * log(float((1 - top) / (1 - p)))
            assert abs(kl - binary) <= LOG_TOLERANCE
            sup = kl_ball_supremum(1, p, kl)
            assert abs(sup - float(top)) <= SUPREMUM_TOLERANCE
            # pi_K is itself the exponential tilt of p0 at t = ln(top (1-p) / ((1-top) p))
            t = log(float(top * (1 - p) / ((1 - top) * p)))
            z = float(1 - p) + float(p) * pow(2.718281828459045, t)
            assert abs(float(p) * pow(2.718281828459045, t) / z - float(top)) <= 1e-12


def test_containment_and_dv_bound_on_a_small_grid():
    for items in (1, 4, 16):
        for candidates in (2, 5, 20):
            for p in GRID_P:
                kl = kl_max_law(items, candidates, p)
                radius = beirami_radius(candidates)
                gap = float(selection_gap(items, candidates, p))
                assert 0 < kl < radius
                assert gap <= dv_bound(items, p, kl) + LOG_TOLERANCE
                assert gap <= dv_bound(items, p, radius) + LOG_TOLERANCE
                assert dv_bound(items, p, radius) <= dv_bound(items, p, radius, "hoeffding") + LOG_TOLERANCE
                assert gap_to_bound_ratio(items, candidates, p) < gaussian_ratio_limit(candidates)
                assert gap_to_bound_ratio(items, candidates, p, "exact") <= 1


def test_gaussian_quadrature_closed_forms_and_c_K():
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(1) - 0) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(2) - 1 / sqrt(pi)) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(3) - 3 / (2 * sqrt(pi))) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(4) - 6 * atan(sqrt(2)) / pi**1.5) <= 1e-9
    for candidates in (2, 3, 5, 10, 100):
        assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(candidates) - gaussian_max_expectation(candidates, "tail")) <= 1e-9
        assert gaussian_max_expectation(candidates) < sqrt(2 * log(candidates))
    values = [gaussian_ratio_limit(k) for k in (2, 3, 5, 10, 100)]
    assert all(0.9 < c < 1 for c in values) and values == sorted(values)
    assert abs(values[0] - (1 / sqrt(pi)) / sqrt(2 * log(2) - 1)) <= 1e-9


def test_kearns_saul_proxy_values_and_grid_sanity():
    assert kearns_saul_proxy(HALF) == 0.25 == hoeffding_proxy()
    for p in (Q(1, 10), QUARTER, Q(2, 5), Q(3, 4)):
        v = kearns_saul_proxy(p)
        assert abs(v - kearns_saul_proxy(1 - p)) <= 1e-15
        assert float(p * (1 - p)) < v < 0.25
        assert subgaussian_violation(p) <= 1e-9
        assert subgaussian_violation(p, "hoeffding") <= 1e-9


def test_uniform_distinct_scores_kl_approaches_the_radius():
    for candidates in (2, 3, 5):
        deficits = [beirami_radius(candidates) - uniform_distinct_scores_kl(n, candidates) for n in (5, 50, 500)]
        assert all(d > 0 for d in deficits) and deficits == sorted(deficits, reverse=True)
        assert deficits[-1] < 1e-4


def test_kl_divergence_handles_tiny_atoms_and_basic_identities():
    tiny = Q(1, 2**4000)
    p0 = {"x": tiny, "y": 1 - tiny}
    pi = {"x": 2 * tiny, "y": 1 - 2 * tiny}
    assert kl_divergence(p0, p0) == 0
    assert 0 < kl_divergence(pi, p0) < 1e-1000 or kl_divergence(pi, p0) >= 0
    assert abs(kl_divergence({"x": Q(1)}, {"x": Q(1)})) == 0
    assert abs(kl_divergence({"x": Q(1), "y": Q(0)}, {"x": HALF, "y": HALF}) - log(2)) <= LOG_TOLERANCE
    assert score_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 1, "b": 1}) == {Q(1): Q(1)}
    assert beirami_radius(1) == 0 and abs(beirami_radius(2) - (log(2) - 0.5)) <= 1e-15


@pytest.mark.parametrize("call", [
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}, 0),
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}, 2.0),
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}, 2, "last_index"),
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 0}, 2),
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": HALF, "b": QUARTER}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}, 2),
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": 0.5, "b": 0.5}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}, 2),
    lambda: selected_record_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 0.0, "b": 1}, 2),
    lambda: selected_record_law({}, {}, 2),
    lambda: brute_force_selected_law({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}, 2, "median"),
    lambda: kl_divergence({"a": Q(1)}, {"b": Q(1)}),
    lambda: kl_divergence({"a": HALF, "b": HALF}, {"a": Q(1), "b": Q(0)}),
    lambda: kl_max_law(0, 2, HALF),
    lambda: kl_max_law(4, 2, Q(0)),
    lambda: kl_max_law(4, 2, Q(1)),
    lambda: kl_max_law(4, 2, 0.5),
    lambda: kearns_saul_proxy(Q(0)),
    lambda: dv_bound(4, HALF, -1.0),
    lambda: dv_bound(4, HALF, 1.0, "bernstein"),
    lambda: kl_ball_supremum(4, HALF, -0.1),
    lambda: gaussian_max_expectation(0),
    lambda: gaussian_max_expectation(2, "moment"),
    lambda: gap_to_bound_ratio(4, 2, HALF, "radius_plus"),
    lambda: uniform_distinct_scores_kl(0, 2),
    lambda: selection_gap(4, 2, Q(3, 2)),
])
def test_malformed_inputs_are_rejected(call):

from fractions import Fraction as Q
from itertools import product
from math import atan, log, pi, sqrt

import pytest

from spiral_ln.evaluation_feedback_multigen import best_of_pmf
from spiral_ln.evaluation_selection_kl import (
    GRID_P, LOG_TOLERANCE, SUPREMUM_TOLERANCE, TIE_RULES, beirami_radius, binomial_records,
    binomial_score_law, brute_force_selected_law, conditioned_on_max_law, dv_bound,
    first_index_weight, gaussian_max_expectation, gaussian_ratio_limit, gap_to_bound_ratio,
    hoeffding_proxy, kearns_saul_proxy, kl_ball_supremum, kl_divergence, kl_max_law, max_law,
    score_law, selected_record_law, selection_gap, subgaussian_violation, uniform_distinct_scores_kl,
    uniform_weight, verify,
)

HALF, QUARTER = Q(1, 2), Q(1, 4)

SPACES = [
    ({"a": Q(1), "b": Q(0)}, {"a": 0, "b": 1}),
    ({"a": Q(1, 3), "b": Q(2, 3)}, {"a": 0, "b": 0}),
    ({"a": Q(1, 2), "b": Q(1, 4), "c": Q(1, 8), "d": Q(1, 8)}, {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 1, "d": 2}),
    ({"a": Q(1, 5), "b": Q(1, 5), "c": Q(1, 5), "d": Q(2, 5)}, {"a": 3, "b": 3, "c": 3, "d": 3}),
    ({"w": Q(1, 10), "x": Q(3, 10), "y": Q(2, 5), "z": Q(1, 5)}, {"w": Q(1, 2), "x": -1, "y": Q(1, 2), "z": 7}),
]


def _enumerate(p0, score, candidates, rule):
    """Independent enumeration over index tuples; the tie rule is applied literally."""

    records = list(p0)
    law = {record: Q(0) for record in records}
    for indices in product(range(len(records)), repeat=candidates):
        weight = Q(1)
        for i in indices:
            weight *= p0[records[i]]
        if weight == 0:
            continue
        top = max(score[records[i]] for i in indices)
        winners = [pos for pos, i in enumerate(indices) if score[records[i]] == top]
        if rule == "first_index":
            law[records[indices[winners[0]]]] += weight
        else:
            share = weight / len(winners)
            for pos in winners:
                law[records[indices[pos]]] += share
    return law


@pytest.mark.parametrize("p0,score", SPACES)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("candidates", [1, 2, 3])
def test_tie_rules_match_enumeration_and_each_other(p0, score, candidates):
    conditioned = conditioned_on_max_law(p0, score, candidates)
    for rule in TIE_RULES:
        closed = selected_record_law(p0, score, candidates, rule)
        assert closed == _enumerate(p0, score, candidates, rule)
        assert closed == brute_force_selected_law(p0, score, candidates, rule)
        assert closed == conditioned
        assert sum(closed.values()) == 1


def test_weights_agree_with_the_geometric_identity():
    for below, upto in ((Q(0), Q(1)), (Q(1, 3), Q(1, 2)), (Q(2, 7), Q(9, 10)), (Q(0), Q(1, 5))):
        for candidates in range(1, 7):
            direct = (upto**candidates - below**candidates) / (upto - below)
            assert first_index_weight(below, upto, candidates) == direct
            assert uniform_weight(below, upto, candidates) == direct


def test_max_law_matches_multigen_best_of_pmf():
    for items, candidates, p in ((2, 2, HALF), (3, 4, QUARTER), (5, 3, Q(2, 3)), (8, 1, HALF)):
        law = max_law(binomial_score_law(items, p), candidates)
        assert [law[Q(j, items)] for j in range(items + 1)] == best_of_pmf(items, candidates, p)
        assert sum(law.values()) == 1


def test_kl_on_records_equals_kl_of_max_law_and_gap_matches_selection_inflation():
    for items in range(1, 7):
        for candidates in (2, 3, 4):
            for p in (HALF, QUARTER, Q(9, 10)):
                p0, score = binomial_records(items, p)
                law = selected_record_law(p0, score, candidates)
                assert abs(kl_divergence(law, p0) - kl_max_law(items, candidates, p)) <= LOG_TOLERANCE
                gap = sum((mass * score[r] for r, mass in law.items()), Q(0)) - p
                assert gap == selection_gap(items, candidates, p)


def test_data_processing_inequality_by_direct_computation():
    p0 = {"a": Q(1, 2), "b": Q(1, 4), "c": Q(1, 8), "d": Q(1, 8)}
    score = {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 1, "d": 2}
    for candidates in (2, 3):
        discrete = selected_record_law(p0, score, candidates)
        discrete_kl = kl_divergence(discrete, p0)
        previous = -1.0
        for levels in (1, 2, 3, 5, 8):
            joint_p0 = {(r, l): m / levels for r, m in p0.items() for l in range(levels)}
            joint_score = {(r, l): Q(score[r]) + Q(l + 1, 2 * (levels + 1)) for (r, l) in joint_p0}
            joint = selected_record_law(joint_p0, joint_score, candidates)
            marginal = {r: Q(0) for r in p0}
            for (r, _), m in joint.items():
                marginal[r] += m
            assert marginal == discrete
            joint_kl = kl_divergence(joint, joint_p0)
            assert joint_kl >= discrete_kl - LOG_TOLERANCE
            assert joint_kl > previous
            assert joint_kl < beirami_radius(candidates)
            previous = joint_kl
        assert beirami_radius(candidates) - previous < 0.01
    # the same inequality for a pair of laws unrelated to selection
    joint_a = {("x", 0): Q(1, 2), ("x", 1): Q(1, 6), ("y", 0): Q(1, 6), ("y", 1): Q(1, 6)}
    joint_b = {("x", 0): Q(1, 4), ("x", 1): Q(1, 4), ("y", 0): Q(1, 4), ("y", 1): Q(1, 4)}
    marginal_a = {"x": Q(2, 3), "y": Q(1, 3)}
    marginal_b = {"x": Q(1, 2), "y": Q(1, 2)}
    assert kl_divergence(marginal_a, marginal_b) <= kl_divergence(joint_a, joint_b)


def test_n_equals_1_gap_equals_kl_ball_supremum_exactly_via_the_tilt():
    for candidates in (2, 3, 5, 10, 20):
        for p in GRID_P:
            top = 1 - (1 - p)**candidates
            assert selection_gap(1, candidates, p) == top - p
            kl = kl_max_law(1, candidates, p)
            binary = float(top) * log(float(top / p)) + float(1 - top) * log(float((1 - top) / (1 - p)))
            assert abs(kl - binary) <= LOG_TOLERANCE
            sup = kl_ball_supremum(1, p, kl)
            assert abs(sup - float(top)) <= SUPREMUM_TOLERANCE
            # pi_K is itself the exponential tilt of p0 at t = ln(top (1-p) / ((1-top) p))
            t = log(float(top * (1 - p) / ((1 - top) * p)))
            z = float(1 - p) + float(p) * pow(2.718281828459045, t)
            assert abs(float(p) * pow(2.718281828459045, t) / z - float(top)) <= 1e-12


def test_containment_and_dv_bound_on_a_small_grid():
    for items in (1, 4, 16):

            for p in GRID_P:
                kl = kl_max_law(items, candidates, p)
                radius = beirami_radius(candidates)
                gap = float(selection_gap(items, candidates, p))
                assert 0 < kl < radius
                assert gap <= dv_bound(items, p, kl) + LOG_TOLERANCE
                assert gap <= dv_bound(items, p, radius) + LOG_TOLERANCE
                assert dv_bound(items, p, radius) <= dv_bound(items, p, radius, "hoeffding") + LOG_TOLERANCE
                assert gap_to_bound_ratio(items, candidates, p) < gaussian_ratio_limit(candidates)
                assert gap_to_bound_ratio(items, candidates, p, "exact") <= 1


def test_gaussian_quadrature_closed_forms_and_c_K():
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(1) - 0) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(2) - 1 / sqrt(pi)) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(3) - 3 / (2 * sqrt(pi))) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_expectation(4) - 6 * atan(sqrt(2)) / pi**1.5) <= 1e-9

    values = [gaussian_ratio_limit(k) for k in (2, 3, 5, 10, 100)]
    assert all(0.9 < c < 1 for c in values) and values == sorted(values)
    assert abs(values[0] - (1 / sqrt(pi)) / sqrt(2 * log(2) - 1)) <= 1e-9

broken by the first index attaining the maximum (*first-index rule*) or uniformly among those attaining it
(*uniform rule*). \(\pi_K\) is the law of the kept record; \(m_K(s)=P(\max_kS(\omega_k)=s)=F(s)^K-F(s-)^K\).
Spiral null: \(\Omega=\{0,1\}^n\), \(p_0=\mathrm{Bern}(p)^n\), \(S=\bar S=\)count\(/n\), and
\(\gamma(n,K,p)=\mathbb E[\max_k\bar S_k]-p=\mathbb E_{\pi_K}[\bar S]-p\) (`selection_inflation`);

and of randomness independent of the sample, with \(J\) in the argmax set. Then

\(P(\omega_J=\omega\mid\text{scores})=p_0(\omega)\mathbf 1\{S(\omega)=\max\}/q(\max)\); take expectations.

(i) *The kept record has law \(\pi_K\).* \(\tilde J\) lies in the discrete argmax set and is a function of the

uniform rule give the same record law.
(ii) *The jittered KL is exactly \(\lambda_K\).* On \(\tilde\Omega=\Omega\times(0,u)\) with
\(\tilde p_0=p_0\otimes\mathrm{Unif}\) and \(\tilde s(\omega,t)=S(\omega)+t\):
\(P((\omega_{\tilde J},U_{\tilde J})\in A)=\sum_kP(X_k\in A,\ \tilde S_k>\tilde S_j\ \forall j\ne k)
=K\int_A\tilde F(\tilde s(x))^{K-1}\tilde p_0(dx)\), so \(d\tilde\pi_K/d\tilde p_0=h:=K\tilde F(\tilde s)^{K-1}\)
and \(\mathrm{KL}(\tilde\pi_K\|\tilde p_0)=\mathbb E_{\tilde\pi_K}\ln h=\ln K+(K-1)\mathbb E\ln V\) with

lemma gives the elementary fallback \(v=\tfrac14\)). For every law \(\pi\ll p_0\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\),

*Proof.* (1) \(\bar S-p=\frac1n\sum_i(X_i-p)\) with independent summands, so

(2) For any \(f\) and \(\pi\ll p_0\), with \(p_0^f\propto e^fp_0\):
\(\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|p_0)+\ln\mathbb E_{p_0}e^f-\mathbb E_\pi f=\mathbb E_\pi\ln\frac{d\pi}{dp_0^f}=\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|p_0^f)\ge0\), equality iff \(\pi=p_0^f\).
(3) Take \(f=t(\bar S-p)\), \(t>0\): \(\mathbb E_\pi[\bar S]-p\le\mathrm{KL}/t+\sigma_n^2t/2\); at

\(p\in\{\tfrac14,\tfrac12,\tfrac34\}\). For \(n\ge2\) the chain \(\gamma<\sup<\sqrt{2\sigma_n^2\mathrm{KL}}\) is

in the score there (\(n=2,K=2,p=\tfrac12\): likelihood ratios \(\tfrac14,1,\tfrac74\)).

## 5. Evidence status and what remains

- *Algebraic identities, every parameter:* Theorems A, B (with strictness and the supremum), C given the proxy; D.1–D.4.
- *Finite verified examples:* the 90-cell grid for B and C; five tie fixtures and \(\{0,1\}^{n\le6}\) for A;

  approach; the strict chain at \(n\ge2\).
- *Cited, not reproved:* the Kearns–Saul inequality (checked on a \(t\)-grid only) and its optimality (attributed,
  unchecked, to Buldygin and Moskvichova 2013 or Berend and Kontorovich 2013); Hoeffding's lemma; de

- Beirami et al.'s bound is no longer load-bearing: Theorem B derives the tie-free value and extends it to the
  tied case, which the crosswalk had left undetermined.
- Open: whether \(r(n,K,\tfrac12)\uparrow c_K\) monotonically in \(n\) for every \(K\); the exact-KL ratio

  was not studied further; everything is under the Spiral null, and the drift chain (crosswalk §8 item 2) is untouched.
